title: Staged weight pipeline and keeper policy to reduce cold-start P99
creator: Anya Patel
description:
Problem: Dedicated tenants are experiencing high P99 request latency during scale-up events and model transitions due to heavyweight model weight loads and cold KV caches. Existing warm-pool strategies reduce average latency but we still see long tail cold starts when: (a) new model variants are staged, (b) weight shards are evicted under memory pressure, or (c) an autoscaler rapidly provisions new nodes for burst traffic.

Goal: Design and implement a staged weight pipeline combined with a \"keeper\" residency policy and adaptive KV priming so we can: (1) reduce cold-start P99 for dedicated capacity by at least 5x for common model families, (2) retain throughput guarantees during burst autoscaling, and (3) minimize additional steady-state memory and cost overhead.

High-level approach: Introduce a three-tier prewarming and residency system: 
1) Staged weight pipeline: weights are published as layered artifacts (light metadata -> memory-mapped delta shards -> fully resident tensors). New nodes perform a fast mmap+on-demand page fault fill for low-latency startup, while a background \"stager\" progressively materializes hot shards to GPU memory prioritized by route heatmaps.
2) Keeper policy: maintain a small, score-based set of residency tokens per GPU pool that prevents eviction of recently hot weights and frequently used routing overlays. Each token has a decaying score that is updated by real traffic and synthetic micro-bursts used for priming.
3) Adaptive KV priming: KV cache priming runs in two modes: selective prefix restore for popular routes (guided by per-route hit-rate telemetry) and lazy micro-rollout priming where a lightweight request generator replays sampled recent prefixes to warm KV entries without full request replication.

Design trade-offs considered: 
- Memory vs latency: Fully keeping all weights resident avoids cold starts but increases footprints and cost. The keeper policy targets a small, high-value set to get most P99 reduction at modest memory cost.
- Predictive vs reactive: Predictive prefetching can misallocate resources; we combine heatmap predictions with conservative canary priming and local traffic signals to avoid wasteful preloads.
- Complexity vs observability: The staged pipeline adds orchestration complexity; we will surface explicit metrics and debugging endpoints to make behavior visible in Console and for on-call use.

Implementation milestones (see implementation_steps for details).
implementation_steps: Design artifact format: introduce 'layered' weight bundle (manifest + mmap-friendly shards + optional eager blobs). Align with model registry schema.
Add mmap loader to node agent with fast path for memory-mapped partial residency and background blob fetcher for GPU DMA uploads.
Implement keeper residency manager per GPU pool: scoring, token assignment, decay policy, and eviction hooks.
Build adaptive KV priming service: route heatmap aggregator, sampler for micro-rollout generator, and a safe priming throttle tied to node SLOs.
Integrate telemetry: priming success rate, keeper hit-rate, cold-start count by model-version, per-node memory overhead, and priming cost counters.
Create rollout plan: canary on a single Dedicated pool, run A/B against baseline for 2 weeks, expand to 50% pools, then global if metrics meet targets.
Console UX: surface priming controls (enable/disable, token budget), per-pool keeper lists, and a priming dashboard.
Testing: unit tests for staged loader, chaos tests evicting shards, load tests with synthetic traffic patterns, and cost analysis for steady-state footprint.
Docs: runbook for on-call, design doc for infra team, and migration notes for existing warm-pool configurations.
acceptance_criteria: P99 cold-start latency for targeted models reduced >= 5x compared to baseline for scale-up events under typical traffic patterns.
No regression in median latency and throughput for steady-state traffic after keeper tokens are activated.
Priming cost (network + memory overhead) stays within configured budget per-pool (configurable; default <= +12% memory, <= +8% network).
Automated priming can be toggled per-pool from Console; feature flag exists for quick rollback.
End-to-end telemetry visible in Console and linked to alerting rules for increased cold-start counts.
metrics: cold_start_p99_ms: tracked by model-version and pool
keeper_hit_rate: fraction of requests served without requiring weight load
priming_success_rate: fraction of priming operations that completed before first real request
priming_traffic_cost_bytes: network bytes used for priming per-pool
steady_state_memory_delta: additional reserved memory per-node after keeper activation
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-priming wastes memory and increases costs. Mitigation: conservative defaults, dynamic budget caps, and telemetry-based throttles.
Risk: Incorrect predictions causing priming for infrequent routes. Mitigation: combine prediction with recent traffic signals and canary priming before global rollout.
Risk: Increased complexity causing harder incidents. Mitigation: observability endpoints, feature flags, and a focused runbook for rollback and diagnosis.
Risk: Security implications of synthetic traffic for priming. Mitigation: ensure priming generator anonymizes inputs and respects tenant data policies; security review required.
